evidence_proposals.excerpt_or_summary: The introduction proposes a linked philosophical system and reports a 1993 web implementation.
The server page says [empty] identifies a menu with no text and reports historical server use.
The overview describes a collaborative philosophy, a conceptual network, and the tools intended to support it.

evidence_proposals.locator: Origin of the Project; (Electronic) Publications; footer
evidence_proposals.excerpt_or_summary: The project history reports a July 1993 web server and a September 1994 experimental adaptive semantic hypertext.
The proposed conceptual network combines nodes, semantic relations, hierarchical access, and formal and informal aspects of meaning.
The page says node types were not really implemented and collaborative status was not fully implemented.
The page lists proposed pragmatic and semantic relations but says only one link type was then implemented.

evidence_proposals.locator: Opening paragraphs; Password and Choose type of annotation fields; footer

The invitation seeks readers, contributors, reviewers, technical help, and administrative support.

nodes.canonical_definition: A collaborative project seeking to develop a cybernetic and evolutionary philosophy with computer support.
nodes.description: The project history attributes the early project to Turchin and Joslyn and reports Heylighen joining the editorial board in 1990. Its overview describes a board, contributors, publications, meetings, and electronic lists. These are dated project self-reports.

nodes.canonical_definition: A hypertext publication and conceptual network associated with the Principia Cybernetica Project.
nodes.description: The project history reports a web server in July 1993 and an experimental adaptive semantic hypertext in September 1994. Its annotation guide describes a historical submission process; present operation was not tested. The server page explains that an [empty] node has a menu but no text.

nodes.canonical_definition: A representation in which nodes are connected by relations whose types can convey meaning.
nodes.description: Joslyn and Heylighen describe a conceptual network with multiple hierarchies and both formal and reader-interpreted meaning. Their technical pages distinguish the proposal from implementation: node types were not really implemented, collaborative status was incomplete, and only one link type was implemented at the time described.

nodes.canonical_definition: An alphabetical index to a composite cybernetics and systems dictionary hosted within the Principia Cybernetica Web.
nodes.description: The index says it combines the ASC Glossary, Krippendorff’s Dictionary, and Hornung’s Glossary with permission, and attributes definitions individually. It credits Francis Heylighen with compilation and hypertext conversion, assisted by An Vranckx.
